_sources.n-23-62: IRS Notice 2023-62, guidance on section 603 of the SECURE 2.0 Act (mandatory Roth catch-up under IRC 414(v)(7)). Recorded for the provenance of two rules rather than for a dollar amount. First, it announces the 2-year administrative transition period that is why rothCatchUpWageThreshold_414v7A is null for catch-up years 2024 and 2025 -- the divergence the reconciled map below asserts. Second, it settles what happens to a catch-up after SECURE 2.0 s.603(b)(1) struck IRC 402(g)(1)(C): "The elimination of section 402(g)(1)(C) of the Code under section 603(b)(1) of the SECURE 2.0 Act does not change this result for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2023" -- the result being that deferrals above the s.402(g)(1)(B) amount stay out of gross income if they satisfy s.414(v). So a valid catch-up does not draw on the s.402(g) limitation and one that fails s.414(v) does. It publishes no annual amount.

1977.iraPolicy_source: The $1,500-or-15-percent rule, exclusion of active participants, and age-70½ restriction remain the ERISA rules. The 1976 Act added the $1,750 joint spousal deduction for taxable years beginning after December 31, 1976.

1981.iraPolicy_source: The IRS Bulletin records that 1981-and-earlier IRA deductions were limited to $1,500 or 15 percent of earned income, while one-earner married couples had a combined IRA limit; it contrasts the 1982 universal-eligibility change for participants covered by an employer plan. The unchanged SEP, §457, and §401(k) fields are the statutory rules enacted by Pub. L. 95-600.

1997.iraPolicy_source: Section 408A applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 1997; the 1997 data therefore has no Roth IRA and no pre-1997 fixed nonworking-spouse or one-earner cap.
1997.sarsep_source: IRS SEP/SARSEP Audit Techniques states that SBJPA prohibited new SARSEPs after December 31, 1996 while pre-1997 SARSEPs could continue.

2008.traditionalCoveredPhaseout_source: Notice 2007-87 publishes the applicable dollar amounts under §219(g)(3)(B)(i) and (ii); each end is the start plus the statutory width in §219(g)(2)(A)(ii), while the married-filing-separately start is the zero amount in §219(g)(3)(B)(iii). See usc-26-219.
2008.traditionalSpouseCoveredPhaseout_source: Notice 2007-87 publishes the joint applicable dollar amount under §219(g)(7)(A); §219(g)(7)(B) supplies the $10,000 width, and a married individual filing separately keeps the zero applicable amount in §219(g)(3)(B)(iii). See usc-26-219.
2008.rothPhaseout_source: Notice 2007-87 publishes the applicable dollar amounts under §408A(c)(3)(C)(ii); each end is the start plus the statutory width in §408A(c)(3)(A)(ii), and the married-filing-separately start is zero under §408A(c)(3)(C)(ii)(III). See usc-26-408A.

2009.rothCatchUpWageThreshold_source: §414(v)(7)(A) was enacted by SECURE 2.0 and is not operative for this year; the table carries the statutory $145,000 base inertly
2009.iraCatchUp50_source: statutory flat $1,000 under §219(b)(5)(B)(ii); not COLA-adjusted before 2024, so absent from the COLA notices
2009.traditionalCoveredPhaseout_source: Notice 2008-102 publishes the applicable dollar amounts under §219(g)(3)(B)(i) (joint return or qualifying widow(er)) and §219(g)(3)(B)(ii) (all other taxpayers other than married filing separately), which are the band starts; unlike the notices from 2013 on it does not print the ranges themselves. Each end is the start plus the width fixed by §219(g)(2)(A)(ii): $10,000, or $20,000 on a joint return. The married-filing-separately start is the zero applicable dollar amount at §219(g)(3)(B)(iii). See usc-26-219.
2009.traditionalSpouseCoveredPhaseout_source: Start from Notice 2008-102 (§219(g)(7)(A)); the end is the start plus the $10,000 width that §219(g)(7)(B) substitutes for §219(g)(2)(A)(ii) in the spouse-covered case. See usc-26-219. The married-filing-separately band is published by no notice. §219(g)(7)(A) replaces only the joint applicable dollar amount, so a married individual filing a separate return keeps the zero fixed by §219(g)(3)(B)(iii), and §219(g)(7)(B) substitutes a $10,000 width for §219(g)(2)(A)(ii). §219(g)(4) removes spouses who lived apart for the whole year from the subsection altogether, which is why the data names this band 'living together'. See usc-26-219.
2009.rothPhaseout_source: Starts from Notice 2008-102, which cites them as §408A(c)(3)(C)(ii)(I) and (II); the same limits are §408A(c)(3)(B)(ii)(I) and (II) in the current Code, a relettering with no change in substance. Each end is the start plus the width fixed by §408A(c)(3)(A)(ii): $15,000, or $10,000 on a joint return or for a married individual filing a separate return, whose applicable dollar amount is zero under §408A(c)(3)(B)(ii)(III). See usc-26-408A.

2023.traditionalSpouseCoveredPhaseout_source: The married-filing-separately band is published by no notice. §219(g)(7)(A) replaces only the joint applicable dollar amount, so a married individual filing a separate return keeps the zero fixed by §219(g)(3)(B)(iii), and §219(g)(7)(B) substitutes a $10,000 width for §219(g)(2)(A)(ii). §219(g)(4) removes spouses who lived apart for the whole year from the subsection altogether, which is why the data names this band 'living together'. See usc-26-219.

2024.starterDeferralOnly_source: Notice 2024-80 states that the 2025 amounts remain $6,000 and $1,000, confirming the initial 2024 statutory amounts.
2024.plesaBalanceCap_source: usc-26-402A. Notice 2023-75 does not state this figure. IRC 402A(e)(3)(A) fixes the limitation at "$2,500" and its flush text directs the Secretary to adjust it only "[i]n the case of contributions made in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024", so 2024 — the first effective year — carries the unadjusted statutory amount rather than an adjusted or carried-forward one.
2024.availabilityPensionLinkedEmergencySaving: usc-26-402A. IRC 402A(e) was added by Pub. L. 117-328, div. T, title I, section 127(e)(1), and section 127(g) applies the amendments to "plan years beginning after December 31, 2023", making 2024 the first year a pension-linked emergency savings account may exist.
2024.traditionalSpouseCoveredPhaseout_source: The married-filing-separately band is published by no notice. §219(g)(7)(A) replaces only the joint applicable dollar amount, so a married individual filing a separate return keeps the zero fixed by §219(g)(3)(B)(iii), and §219(g)(7)(B) substitutes a $10,000 width for §219(g)(2)(A)(ii). §219(g)(4) removes spouses who lived apart for the whole year from the subsection altogether, which is why the data names this band 'living together'. See usc-26-219.

2025.rothCatchUpWageThreshold_note: Notice 2024-80 calls this 'the Roth catch-up wage threshold for 2024', applied to 2024 wages to determine whether 2025 catch-up contributions must be Roth. Keyed here by the CATCH-UP year, matching the repository convention.
2025.plesaBalanceCap_source: n-24-80: "The limitation under section 402A(e)(3)(A)(i) concerning pension-linked emergency savings accounts that may be included in certain types of defined contribution plans remains $2,500."
2025.traditionalSpouseCoveredPhaseout_source: The married-filing-separately band is published by no notice. §219(g)(7)(A) replaces only the joint applicable dollar amount, so a married individual filing a separate return keeps the zero fixed by §219(g)(3)(B)(iii), and §219(g)(7)(B) substitutes a $10,000 width for §219(g)(2)(A)(ii). §219(g)(4) removes spouses who lived apart for the whole year from the subsection altogether, which is why the data names this band 'living together'. See usc-26-219.

2026.rothCatchUpWageThreshold_note: Notice 2025-67 calls this 'the Roth catch-up wage threshold for 2025', applied to 2025 wages to determine whether 2026 catch-up contributions must be Roth. Keyed here by the CATCH-UP year, matching the repository convention.
2026.plesaBalanceCap_source: n-25-67: "The limitation under section 402A(e)(3)(A)(i) concerning pension-linked emergency savings accounts that may be included in certain types of defined contribution plans is increased from $2,500 to $2,600."

_electiveDeferralComment: Section 402(g)(1) and section 457(e)(15) have been identical in every year listed. 2013 and 2014 are established by IR-2013-86 ('remains unchanged at $17,500' for 2014, which fixes 2013 at the same amount); 2015 by IR-2014-99; 2016 onward by the named notice.
